name: Senior Resources Agency on Aging (Norwich)
description: Connecticut’s five Area Agencies on Aging serve lists of towns. They help older adults, people with disabilities and caregivers with information, benefits counseling, caregiver support and in-home services.
next_step: Call and describe what is hard right now. Ask for information and assistance. The statewide CHOICES line, 1-800-994-9422, also reaches the agency serving your town. Military service is not required.
constraints: Many services focus on people age 60 and older and adults with disabilities; eligibility and waitlists vary by program.
This agency also serves Columbia, Coventry, Mansfield, Union and Willington (Tolland County).

name: Connecticut Long Term Care Ombudsman Program
organization: Connecticut Long Term Care Ombudsman Program
description: The regional long-term care ombudsman for this county: advocacy for residents of nursing homes, assisted living and residential care facilities.
next_step: Call the regional ombudsman program. Give the facility name and county. For immediate danger, call 911.
constraints: The ombudsman acts with the resident’s permission and is not a licensing or enforcement agency.
Regional ombudsmen are assigned by town; the same numbers reach yours. Office: 860-424-5200.

source_evidence.title: Connecticut Long Term Care Ombudsman Program
source_evidence.scope: Toll-free 1-866-388-1888; read in full; undated. Regional ombudsmen are assigned by town, and all share the program number 860-424-5200 (https://portal.ct.gov/LTCOP/Content/Contact-Us/All-Regions; search excerpt), so every county shows the statewide line.
